transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist here. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, doctor... I'm here because I've been having some thoughts that really scared me. I haven't tried to hurt myself or anything like that, but lately I just keep thinking that it would be a relief if I just went to sleep and didn't wake up. It's been bothering me enough that I figured I should come talk to someone about it.
When did you first start having these thoughts about not waking up? Was it sudden, or did it develop gradually over time?
Well, it wasn't sudden. It's been going on for about four months now. It started right around the time my aunt came to live with us.
Besides these thoughts about not waking up, have you been feeling persistently sad, empty, or down most days over these past four months?

Yes, I have. Um... most mornings, I wake up with this heavy sadness right in my chest. It's just... it feels like I already failed the day before it even starts. So, yes, that feeling has been there pretty much every day.
Before these four months, have you ever experienced a period like this where you felt depressed or down for most of the day, nearly every day, lasting at least two weeks?

No, I haven't. I mean, I've had bad days or maybe a bad week here and there, just like anybody else, I suppose. But nothing like this... nothing that lasted for weeks on end or felt this heavy. This is the first time it's been this bad for this long.
Over these past four months, have you found that things you normally enjoy doing—hobbies, time with friends, activities you used to like—have stopped being enjoyable or interesting to you?

Yes, that's exactly what's happened. I used to really look forward to doing my watercolors... and I had a dance class, plus I'd go walking with some ladies from the neighborhood. But lately, I just leave my painting things sitting there on the table. I can't even make myself care about any of it anymore.
Over these past four months, have you noticed any changes in your sleep? For instance, are you sleeping more than usual, or are you having trouble falling asleep or staying asleep?

No, not really. My sleep has been about the same as it always is. I don't have much trouble falling asleep, and I'm not sleeping during the day or anything like that. I sleep my normal hours... it's just that when I do wake up, I have that heavy feeling I told you about. But the sleeping itself is fine.
Over these past four months, have you noticed any changes in your appetite or your weight?
No, my appetite has been pretty steady. I still eat my regular meals, and my weight hasn't really changed that I've noticed. My clothes still fit the same. So no, nothing different there.
Over these past four months, have you been feeling worthless or excessively guilty about things—either things you've done or things you feel you should have done?

Yes, I do get those feelings. Um... especially with my aunt. Sometimes I get really tired, or I just get annoyed with her. And when I do, I start thinking that I'm just a bad woman. I feel like I'm bringing shame on my family because I should be more grateful, you know? It just makes me feel awful about myself.
Over these past four months, have you been feeling unusually tired or fatigued most days, even when you've had enough sleep?

Yes, I do. Even after a full night in bed, my body just feels worn out. It's like... well, just doing regular things, like carrying the laundry or making breakfast, it takes a lot more out of me than it should. I just feel really drained most days.
Over these past four months, have you noticed that you're moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or have others mentioned that you seem to be slowing down?

Yeah, my husband has actually brought that up. He says I move like... well, like everything just takes extra effort now. And I guess I notice it, too. Even when I go to the market, I'll just stand there way too long before finally picking up what I came for. I'm just not as quick as I used to be.
Over these past four months, have you noticed that it's harder for you to concentrate or focus on things, or that making decisions—even small ones—has become more difficult?

No, I haven't really noticed any problems with that. I mean, I can still focus on things fine, and making decisions doesn't seem any harder than it usually is. I just... I haven't had any trouble with my concentration.
Over these past four months, have you ever heard voices or seen things that other people couldn't hear or see, or have you had any unusual beliefs that others around you didn't share?

Well, yes, actually. Um... sometimes when the house is real quiet, usually after I put my aunt to bed, I hear my mother's voice. It's clear as day. She tells me that I'm selfish, or that I'm just not doing enough. And... well, the thing is, I know she's been gone for years, but I still hear her saying those things to me.
Besides hearing your mother's voice, have you had any other unusual experiences—like believing things that others don't believe, or feeling like people are watching you or trying to harm you?
No, I haven't had anything like that. I don't feel like anyone is watching me or out to get me, and I don't have any strange beliefs. It's just the voice I hear sometimes.

When you hear your mother's voice telling you that you're selfish or not doing enough, do you recognize at that moment that it's not really her, but rather something happening because of how depressed you've been feeling?

Well... I'm not really sure. I mean, like I said, I know she's gone, so I know she's not actually standing in the room with me. But I never really thought about it being because I'm depressed. 

When it happens, it just sounds so real, and... well, I just feel terrible hearing it. I haven't really thought about why it's happening, to be honest. I just know it's her voice.
When you hear your mother's voice, does this always happen when you're fully awake and going about your day, or does it sometimes happen when you're falling asleep or just waking up?

Well, I'm fully awake. It's not when I'm in bed or drifting off to sleep or anything like that. Like I mentioned, it usually happens right after I put my aunt to bed, so I'm just sitting up in the living room... completely awake. That's when I hear it.
